# PR Size and Stacked Delivery

Governing thought: Deliver one complete, reviewable change per PR, aiming for 600 changed lines or fewer and building dependent work through verified GitHub stacks.

> Drift check: Check the [GitHub stacking documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/get-started/about-stacked-prs), the [gh-stack skill](https://github.com/github/gh-stack/blob/main/skills/gh-stack/SKILL.md), and `gh stack <command> --help` before stack operations; preview behavior and flags can change.

## Rules (RFC 2119)

- Each PR **MUST** deliver one logical change that can be understood and validated against its base without relying on a future PR. Why: Reviewers need a complete unit of reasoning.
- Authors **SHOULD** target 600 changed lines or fewer per PR, with smaller changes welcome. Why: This is a reviewability target, not a quota or automatic rejection threshold.
- Authors **MUST** measure logical review size as additions plus deletions against the PR's immediate base, including tests and documentation but excluding autogenerated lockfile changes. Why: Dependency-resolution churn does not represent additional authored logic to review.
- Authors **MUST** report excluded lockfile churn separately from logical review size. Why: The raw diff stays transparent without triggering a size exception solely for generated lockfiles.
- Authors **MUST** verify lockfile provenance through independent regeneration from reviewed dependency inputs and approved package sources before taking the content-review exemption. Why: An edited download URL is not trustworthy merely because it appears in a generated file.
- A PR above 600 changed lines **MAY** remain intact when it is one coherent change and splitting would make correctness or review harder. Why: Logical completeness matters more than arithmetic.
- Authors exceeding the target **MUST** explain the size, why a useful split is worse, and a concrete review path in the PR description. Why: Reviewers can assess the exception on evidence.
- Reviewers **MUST** assess logical scope, complexity, file spread, and validation evidence before accepting a size exception. Why: Neither a small count nor an exception guarantees an easy review.
- Authors **MUST** keep the tests, necessary documentation, and consumer updates required by a behavior or contract change in the same PR. Why: A later layer cannot repair an incomplete earlier layer.
- Authors **MUST NOT** meet the target by removing tests, compressing readable code, hiding changed files, or creating unused abstractions or temporary stubs solely to divide work. Why: Size discipline protects quality.
- Authors **MUST** plan multi-PR work before implementation as ordered outcomes with dependencies, estimated sizes, validation, and landing intent. Why: Writing everything first makes later splitting expensive.
- Dependent changes **SHOULD** use native GitHub stacked pull requests through `gh stack`. Why: Stack order represents actual dependencies.
- Independent changes **SHOULD** use separate PRs or stacks. Why: Unrelated work does not belong in a dependency chain.
- Agents working with stacks **MUST** read and use the installed `gh-stack` skill and its `references/stack-design.md`, or read the linked upstream versions if unavailable locally. Why: The skill covers placement, non-interactive commands, and recovery.
- Authors **MUST** satisfy the advancement gate below for the current PR before creating or implementing the next dependent layer. Why: Feedback is incorporated before more work depends on it.
- Authors **MUST** re-establish that gate for affected layers after a push, rebase, base change, or new review feedback invalidates the evidence. Why: Earlier results do not prove the current revision is ready.
- Authors **MUST** self-review every changed line except autogenerated lockfile contents, verify generated suggestions against repository behavior, and remove unrelated cleanup, speculative generalization, redundant comments, and unsupported claims. Why: Generated volume is not evidence of correctness.
- Stack merges **MUST** preserve all applicable checks, approvals, and resolved-feedback requirements for every included PR. Why: Grouped landing does not waive per-PR review.

## Scope and Audience

All human contributors and agents planning, implementing, reviewing, or landing changes. This file is the canonical policy for PR size and stack progression; specialized workflows add their own acceptance criteria.

## At-a-Glance Quick-Start

1. State this PR's outcome in one sentence; separate unrelated work.
2. Plan dependent outcomes bottom to top, including tests and documentation in each estimate.
3. Implement and submit only the current layer; inspect its diff against its immediate parent.
4. Pass the advancement gate, then start the next layer. A ready parent can remain open for grouped landing.
5. Recheck every included PR before merging a ready prefix or the whole stack.

## Core Principles

- Reviewability is the goal; 600 lines is Mississippi's target, not an externally proven optimum.
- A working layer includes its prerequisites and its proof; it does not depend on code above it.
- One active implementation layer per dependency chain keeps review feedback manageable.

## Planning and Size Judgment

For a small change, a short task note is enough. For a stack, record each layer's outcome, immediate base, scope, size estimate, tests/docs, and whether to land separately or together. Prefer a small end-to-end behavior or a useful preparatory refactor over arbitrary file-count or technical-layer splits. Keep coupled changes together when separating them obscures correctness.

Use `git diff <base>...HEAD --stat` and `git diff <base>...HEAD --numstat` with the actual PR base. Report logical review size excluding autogenerated lockfiles, the excluded lockfile churn, and the raw total. For example, 250 source/test lines plus 1,000 autogenerated lockfile lines is a 250-line logical review and needs no size exception for the lockfile churn. Explain other generated output, mechanical moves, large deletions, and binary changes separately. AI-written source still counts toward review size.

Verified autogenerated lockfile contents do not require line-by-line code review. Independently regenerate them in a clean workspace from reviewed manifests, intended version selections, and approved registry/source configuration, without trusting the submitted lockfile as the generation input. Compare the result with the submitted lockfile: unexplained differences or unverified package sources fail validation and block merge until resolved. Successful restore/build alone does not prove provenance. Keep the generated lockfiles in the PR and run applicable restore/build checks; their churn remains excluded from logical review size.

For example, a 720-line contract rename with all consumers and tests updated can be clearer as one PR; explain the mechanical transformation and validation. A 350-line bug fix mixed with an unrelated feature still needs splitting. Neither example is automatic approval.

## Advancement Gate

Before starting the next dependent PR, verify on GitHub for the current head and relevant base:

- All applicable CI/CD jobs have completed successfully, including required checks and deployment checks that run for PRs. Pending, failed, canceled, missing, or unexpectedly skipped jobs are not a pass; explain intentional non-applicability.
- Required reviews and CODEOWNER approvals are present, with no outstanding changes requested.
- Every review comment has a disposition and every review thread is resolved, including bot and outdated threads. Fixes have been pushed and verified; declined suggestions or agreed follow-ups have reviewer agreement. Acknowledging praise does not require a code change.
- The description, scope, size rationale if needed, and validation evidence match the current diff.

Record the PR link, checked head/base revisions, CI results, and review/thread status in the task handoff. A quiet poll or a local completion marker is not approval. If review, credentials, CI, or thread permissions block the gate, report the exact blocker and leave the next layer unstarted. Planning later layers can continue; implementing them waits. See [review polling](pr-review-polling.instructions.md) for remediation mechanics.

After a lower-layer correction, edit the owning branch, propagate it up the stack with the skill's rebase/sync workflow, and recheck affected layers before advancing or merging. Each layer remains buildable and testable with its ancestors; keep incomplete user-facing functionality disabled where necessary for safe independent landing.

## GitHub and gh-stack Workflow

GitHub's native stacked PRs were announced in public preview on July 30, 2026; documentation checked September 8, 2026. They form a linear chain within one repository; cross-fork stacks are unsupported. The bottom PR targets the trunk (usually `main`); later PRs target the preceding branch. GitHub applies the trunk's review protections and PR CI to every native layer. Verify actual jobs and rules on the repository rather than treating absent checks as success. See [GitHub's rollout guide](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/tutorials/roll-out-stacked-prs).

Install the official extension with `gh extension install github/gh-stack`. Agents also use the [gh-stack skill and supporting references](https://github.com/github/gh-stack/tree/main/skills/gh-stack); this is distinct from installing the CLI extension. Read [stack design](https://github.com/github/gh-stack/blob/main/skills/gh-stack/references/stack-design.md) before choosing layers. Follow repository branch names and specify the intended remote when needed by the skill.

Example sequence (replace topic, branch, remote, and PR placeholders with verified values):

```powershell
gh stack init codex/topic/first-change
# Implement this layer, stage its files deliberately, commit, and validate.
gh stack submit --auto --remote origin
gh stack view --json
# Update the generated PR title/body using the repository template.
# Mark ready for review; wait for the full advancement gate above.
gh stack add codex/topic/next-change
# Implement and validate this next layer, then submit and repeat the gate.
gh stack submit --auto --remote origin
```

`submit --auto` submits the stack and creates new PRs as drafts; `--open` creates them ready for review. Use `gh stack view --json` and explicit branch/target arguments for agents; avoid interactive menus. Verify native stack membership as the chain grows. If native stacks are unavailable, report the limitation and use small standalone PRs with dependencies merged first; do not assume manually chained bases inherit native stack protections.

Once the included layers pass their gates and merge is authorized, use `gh stack merge <pr-number-or-stack-number> --yes`. A PR target includes that PR and all unmerged ancestors; a stack target includes the entire stack. Confirm the target and merge method first. This supports landing reviewed changes together without replacing them with one giant PR. Merge queues may land separate groups, so grouped merge is not an atomic deployment guarantee. See the [official skill's merge guidance](https://github.com/github/gh-stack/blob/main/skills/gh-stack/SKILL.md#merging).

## Evidence and References

These sources inform the policy; the 600-line target and sequential advancement gate are Mississippi decisions. Google and GitHub also describe concurrent dependent work, which this repository deliberately gates on completed review.

| Source | Practice applied here |
|--------|-----------------------|
| [Google: Small CLs](https://google.github.io/eng-practices/review/developer/small-cls.html) | One self-contained change, related tests together, plan splits early, exercise judgment about size. |
| [Google: What to look for in a code review](https://google.github.io/eng-practices/review/reviewer/looking-for.html) | Check design, complexity, tests, and documentation; avoid speculative functionality. |
| [Google: Handling reviewer comments](https://google.github.io/eng-practices/review/developer/handling-comments.html) | Address feedback with evidence and improve the code's explanation, not just the review conversation. |
| [GitLab Handbook: Iteration](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/workflow/iteration/) | Choose useful incremental changes; keep coupled behavior together when technical-layer splits hide context. |
| [GitHub: Native stacks announcement](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-30-stacked-pull-requests-are-now-in-public-preview/) | Review individual layers and land ready changes together. |
| [GitHub: Stacking agent-generated changes](https://github.blog/engineering/turn-one-giant-ai-generated-pull-request-to-a-reviewable-stack/) | Teach agents stack design and the official tooling before implementation. |
